title: Call Conductor: cross-SDK schema adapter and invocation ergonomics
creator: Miguel Rivera
description:
Goal: Implement a "call conductor" library in the Redwood SDKs (Python / TypeScript / Go) that provides a consistent, ergonomic surface for function/tool calling. The module will: validate model-provided function schemas, coerce/normalize arguments, orchestrate streaming or non-streaming invocations, attach idempotency and retry metadata, and emit structured telemetry.

Why: Current SDK helpers are fragmented across languages and lack a single canonical strategy for handling schema drift, partial streaming results, and retry semantics. This causes duplicated logic in apps, surprising runtime failures when models return slightly different schemas, and inconsistent developer ergonomics.

Scope: 1) API surface (sync/async wrappers, streaming iterator helpers, typed adapters) 2) Schema validation modes (strict | permissive | noop) with migration path 3) Adaptive retry/backoff with idempotency and durable dedup keys 4) Stream resume checkpoints and example strategies for resumable partial results 5) Cross-language examples and cookbook entries for common patterns (validation-first, fallback-to-text, best-effort-coercion) 6) Telemetry hooks (span attributes, event counters for SchemaMismatch/InvocationError/StreamResume)

Non-goals: opinionated language-level typing libraries; heavy runtime payload transformations (beyond normalization/coercion); changing server-side contract enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a CallConductor API that performs schema validation + invocation with the same behavioral modes across languages; 2) Schema validation modes are configurable at call-time and via global SDK config; 3) Streaming invocations provide a resumable iterator and clear error types; 4) Retry behavior supports idempotency key attachment and safe-at-most-once vs at-least-once options; 5) Examples exist in Python, TS, and Go repos demonstrating a) strict validation with early rejection, b) permissive validation with best-effort coercion, c) streaming resume, and d) fallback-to-raw-text path; 6) End-to-end tests validate telemetry events and contract-level metrics; 7) No regressions in existing unit tests and CI is green; 8) Migration doc and changelog entry authored in the SDK docs.
design_decisions:
- Provide three validation modes: strict (reject on mismatch), permissive (coerce/strip unknown fields), noop (skip validation).
- Validation should be performed using a normalized intermediate representation to handle model-provided variations (string enums vs symbols, nested optional fields, extra top-level keys).
- Streaming paths return an async iterator (or language equivalent) that yields {event_type, payload, checkpoint_token?} tuples; checkpoint_token is opaque to SDK consumer but persisted by apps for resume.
- Retries are split into transient (network, 429, 503) and semantic (schema-mismatch during commit); only transient errors use automatic transparent retry with backoff. Schema-mismatch will surface to caller unless permissive mode enabled.
- Idempotency: callers can supply an idempotency key; the CallConductor will also synthesize one from a stable hash of (user_api_key, model_name, function_name, normalized_args) when not provided.
- Telemetry hooks should be pluggable; default emits span attributes to Redwood tracing and counters for SchemaMismatch, RetryAttempt, InvocationSuccess, StreamResume.
- Language ergonomics: keep API names consistent across SDKs (CallConductor.call, CallConductor.stream, CallConductor.validate). Avoid overloading method signatures aggressively—prefer explicit call options object to keep bindings stable across languages.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: validation rules, coercion heuristics, idempotency key generation, retry/backoff behavior, stream iterator semantics.
- Integration tests: end-to-end against the runtime with recorded model fixtures that intentionally return schema variants (extra fields, missing optional keys, type mismatches).
- Fuzz tests: feed randomized schemas and assert conductor never throws native exceptions (returns structured errors).
- Performance: microbenchmarks to ensure conductor adds <2ms median overhead to non-streaming invocations and <5% overhead on streaming throughput.
- QA: manual verification by SDK leads (Sofia Martinez) running sample apps and verifying telemetry counters on staging dashboards.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch + cross-SDK API prototype (week 1) 2) Integration tests + perf microbenchmarks (week 2) 3) Docs + cross-language examples and PRDs published (week 3) 4) Canary release: enable permissive validation by default behind a feature flag for 10% of traffic on hosted API and SDK beta pinning (week 4) 5) Gradual release: flip flag to default permissive for SDK minor, document strict mode for maximal safety (week 5).
Rollback: toggle feature flag in SDK config + deprecate synthesized idempotency key behavior if issues found.
comments: 2026-03-06 Miguel Rivera (creator): Initial ticket created after sync with SDK leads. Scope and acceptance criteria drafted. Asked for runtime input on resume tokens and idempotency semantics.

2026-03-08 Priya Patel (assignee): Prototype sketched for Python and TS. Decided to lift heavy validation logic into a shared canonical module to avoid duplication. Raised question: should synthesized idempotency include model revision? Added to design decisions.

2026-03-10 Jonah Lee (runtime): Runtime will expose a lightweight resume token in streaming responses (opaque bytes). We recommend using token TTL of 24h. Also flagged potential privacy concern for synthesized idempotency keys; suggested hashing + pepper per-customer.

2026-03-11 Sofia Martinez (SDK lead): Reviewed API sketches. Requested explicit CallOptions object to avoid cross-language signature drift. Requested cookbook examples for fallback-to-text and strict-reject patterns.

2026-03-12 Ethan Chen (security): Security review requested. Noted that synthesized idempotency keys must not leak PII; require deterministic hashing and KMS-managed pepper. Marked for security gating before release.

2026-03-14 Priya Patel: Implemented Python prototype and unit tests for schema coercion heuristics. Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482. Running microbenchmarks; median added latency ~1.7ms. Planned to land TS and Go variants next week.
